Oh, that reminds me of a story, which I'll tell as quickly as I can but as strange as it is, it was a day that made a big impact on me:

One day about 14 years ago, I got a knock on the front door and responded. It was a neighbor, and he asked me if the black kitten under the SUV across the street belonged to me. I said no, and he said he was checking around and if nobody claimed him, he was gonna take him to the animal shelter and then went to the next house to ask them.

This interested me and I wanted to see the kitten at least, as a crowd about a dozen people had started to gather to look. I figured I'd walk over, look, and come back in, no big deal.

When I got to the far side of the street, I saw this shadowy-black figure moving around but hard to see much because it was a black kitten under the SUV in the shadows. He dipped his head to see who I was, and I saw two beautiful gold eyes for a moment, then they disappeared again when he stood up. I figured that was that, and that I hoped he found a nice home, but I had a cat (Ernie) as it was.

Weelllllll....the kitten had other ideas, apparently. He saw me, stood up, then STROLLED OUT like he owned the entire place....in ABSOLUTELY no hurry. He took a path to stay as far away from everyone as he possibly could while making his way my direction. He wound up coming right up to me, then sat about 6 inches away from the ends of my toes, and then looked up at me right in the eyes as if to say, "Well? What are you waiting for? I have arrived!"

I stood there, dumbfounded at the fearlessness of this ~ 10 week old kitten (JUST weaned, apparently) as well as his strong will and so I picked him up and took him home. He has ruled the roost ever since, and it turns out he's by FAR AND AWAY the most intelligent, craftiest little sneak I've ever encountered.

About a week later, I took him to the vet to get checked out. "Clyde" - the kitten - fought the vet, tooth and nail. The vet and I went to the same college, 2 states away, and are friends from way back, and he's the best vet around. Poor Chuck did his best to examine him and Clyde would NOT cooperate. Finally, the vet got what he could from the exam, Clyde turned his back and stalked away, slowly in his "Joe Cool" fashion. Chuck looked after him for a beat or two, turned to me, and said, "THAT one has a REALLY high opinion of himself, doesn't he?"

I lost it. He had nailed Clyde's personality in one statement.

Subsequent visits only got worse and worse as Clyde grew up and got bigger and stronger. He'd get all upset when he knew we were going to the vet...all other cats, I could hand-carry inside even with dogs and cats around. Ernie used to rest in my lap in the waiting area, but Clyde I had to use a cat carrier. The staff wondered too, saying "All your others over the years have always been so SWEET..."

One visit, Chuck made a horrendous mistake; he turned his back on Clyde. Clyde took the opportunity to bite his hand. HARD. Sunk his fangs deep. To his credit, Chuck wasn't mad at all, he even said it was his own fault and that Clyde was a crafty one. The following visit, Chuck had figured it out; Clyde was a 1st-gen "feral" cat. You would NEVER know it, either. He's more calm, cool, and collected than any cat I've ever had.

Except when he's at the vet, then he goes all Halloween Cat, but in his geriatric years, he's mellowed to a degree...now, he usually isn't foaming at the mouth until the visit is either over or almost over.

So, don't worry about a long story about your Finn. I enjoyed reading it and was sad at the same time...enjoyed reading about the bond and the love, but sad to know he's no longer around.
